verses.text: Now about food offered to idols. We know that "we all have knowledge." But knowledge makes people proud, while love builds people up.
Anyone who thinks they know something does not yet know as they should.
But whoever loves God is known by God.
So about eating food offered to idols: we know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is only one God.
There may be so-called gods in heaven or on earth. In fact, there are many "gods" and many "lords".
But for us there is only one God, the Father. All things come from him, and we live for him. And there is only one Lord, Jesus Christ. All things were made through him, and we live through him.
But not everyone knows this. Some people are still so used to idols that when they eat this food, they think of it as offered to an idol. Their conscience is weak, so they feel unclean.
Food does not bring us closer to God. We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
But be careful that your freedom does not cause someone with a weaker faith to fall.
Suppose someone with a weak conscience sees you, who know better, eating in an idol's temple. Will they not be encouraged to eat food offered to idols?
So this weak believer, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
When you sin against your brothers and sisters like this and hurt their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
So if what I eat causes a believer to fall into sin, I will never eat meat again. I do not want to cause them to fall.
